findings.description: The EC2 instance's user_data script embeds a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMAAAKEY). User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service and is also visible in the AWS console/API and Terraform state, so these long-lived credentials must be treated as compromised.

The security group allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration of the portal server to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks. SSH should be restricted to known administrative CIDR ranges or reached via a bastion/SSM.

The security group allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0. Combined with the public subnet and automatic public IP assignment, the Apache web service is directly reachable from the internet over cleartext HTTP with no fronting control (load balancer, WAF, or restricted CIDR).

The egress rule permits all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving the instance unrestricted outbound connectivity that facilitates data exfiltration and command-and-control communication if the instance is compromised.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true and the subnet is associated with a route table containing a 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway, so instances launched here (including the portal server whose security group exposes SSH to 0.0.0.0/0) receive public IPs and are directly internet-facing with no network boundary in front of them.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true and the subnet is associated with the route table that has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway, so instances launched here automatically receive public IP addresses and are exposed to the internet.
The EBS volume attached to the portal server has no encrypted setting, so data written to the disk is stored unencrypted at rest and can be read if the underlying storage or snapshots are accessed.

The EBS snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume with no encryption specified, so the backup contents are stored unencrypted at rest and can be restored or shared without an encryption boundary.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving network traffic metadata (source/destination IPs, ports, and action) stored unencrypted at rest.
